ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the per-phase equivalent circuit of an induction motor. The input on the left is Vs, in series with a 0.04 Ω resistor and j0.22 Ω leakage reactance; from the middle node to the lower common line is the excitation branch, labeled j6.28 Ω, and the air-gap voltage Vg is marked across the two ends of this branch; the rotor branch on the right starts from this node, in series with j0.22 Ω and a resistance of 0.05/s Ω. Reasoning: The problem gives Vg = 210 V rms, s = 0.05, frequency f = 50 Hz, number of poles P = 2, three-phase operation. According to the specified method, the rotor referred resistance is R2'/s = 0.05/0.05 = 1 Ω, therefore the rotor branch impedance Z2 = 1 + j0.22 Ω. The square of the rotor current magnitude is |I2'|^2 = Vg^2 / |Z2|^2 = 210^2 / (1^2 + 0.22^2) = 44100 / 1.0484 ≈ 42064.1 A^2. The total air-gap power is P_ag = 3 |I2'|^2 (R2'/s) = 3 × 42064.1 × 1 ≈ 126192 W. The synchronous speed of two-pole, 50 Hz is ns = 120f/P = 3000 rpm = 50 rps, so the synchronous angular speed ωs = 2π × 50 ≈ 314.16 rad/s. The electromagnetic torque T = P_ag / ωs ≈ 126192 / 314.16 ≈ 401.64 N·m.
